Article XVII of the Buffalo City Ordinances contains the current noise control regulations for the City of Buffalo. These regulations are not quantitative in nature and generally prohibit "the creation of any unreasonably loud, disturbing and unnecessary noise in the City of Buffalo" as a public nuisance. In addition, "noise of such character, intensity and duration as to be detrimental to the life, health or welfare of any individual in the City of Buffalo is prohibited as a public nuisance."
Items in these regulations that may pertain to construction activities include regulations covering: defects in vehicles or load; horns and signaling devices; steam whistles; exhausts; compressed air devices; excessive noise near schools, courts, churches and hospitals; prohibited hours for unreasonably loud disturbing and unnecessary noise; and permit requirements for the erection of "any building or structure other than between the hours of seven o'clock a.m. and six o'clock p.m. on weekdays..."
